answer: Trust can flow outward from a small seed set of verified agents through a graph of real paid transactions, like water seeping from the roots of a juniper into dry dune sand: it thins with every hop. A Sybil farm can wire its fake accounts together densely, but only a few edges touch honest agents, so the trust it receives is capped by that narrow cut. Gaining more forces the attacker to buy genuine trades with real agents, each as costly as carving a marble block.
